evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/manifest.py:284 `f"{_REVIEW_PHASE_PREFIX} {phase_metadata['phase']}",` — build_manifest unconditionally emits a review-phase token, so no legacy phase-absent manifest can be produced via this helper

docs/release-notes.md: 'Legacy attestations with no material pins remain compatible' — this CLOSE-path compatibility claim has no exercising test (ABSENCE: no test builds a phase-token-absent manifest and drives it through `transition ... closed` under enforced+require_plan_review_for_close)
advisory.finding: The CHANGELOG and release-notes assert legacy unpinned attestations 'remain compatible', but no new test exercises a truly phase-token-absent legacy manifest through the CLOSE gate. build_manifest always emits a 'review-phase:' token (manifest.py:284), so the dogfood helper _legacy_plan_attestation produces a phase-aware planning manifest, and it is only exercised at claim — the documented close-time back-compat guarantee is unverified.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Rename the helper/test to reflect it covers a phase-aware unpinned planning review, not a legacy phase-absent manifest.
evidence: tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py:115 `review_phase="planning",` with `pins=()` — 'unpinned' (no pins) but NOT legacy (has a phase token)
advisory.finding: The dogfood test and helper named 'legacy unpinned' actually construct and verify a phase-aware planning review (empty pins but a present review-phase token), which is misleading about what compatibility surface is covered.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CLOSE-profile test with enforcement on for a plan-review manifest that has NO `review-phase:` token, asserting it remains valid (legacy close compatibility preserved).
evidence: attest.py:552-557: `if (profile is PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE and enforced and signed_phase == "planning" and has_phase_metadata): phase_status = "incompatible"`
attest.py:529: `has_phase_metadata = any(str(line).startswith("review-phase: ") for line in auth_manifest)`

tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_policy_dogfood.py:111-116 — `_legacy_plan_attestation` builds the manifest WITH `review_phase="planning"`, so it carries a phase token and is not a genuinely legacy (no-token) manifest; it is used only by test_legacy_unpinned_attestation_claims_through_real_cli (a CLAIM test), never a close.

ABSENCE: search over tests/unit/test_plan_review_close_gate_heldout.py for `review-phase` returns no matches; the new unit test test_plan_review_phase_validity.py builds `_manifest(phase="planning")` (has token) so it only exercises the phase-aware branch, never the legacy no-token CLOSE-under-enforcement path.
CHANGELOG.md: 'legacy unpinned attestations remain accepted.' and release-notes.md: 'Legacy attestations with no material pins remain compatible'
advisory.finding: The legacy-compatibility close path under material-pin enforcement is untested: no test drives a truly legacy plan-review attestation (one with NO `review-phase:` token) through the CLOSE profile with enforcement on. The new code guards this exact case with `and has_phase_metadata` (attest.py:534-538 and 552-557) precisely to keep legacy close-review attestations passing, and the CHANGELOG/release-notes explicitly promise 'legacy unpinned attestations remain accepted' / 'legacy attestations with no material pins remain compatible', yet if that guard were removed a legacy no-token close would silently flip to incompatible-phase with no failing test.
scenarios: A downstream/legacy plan-review manifest lacking a `review-phase:` line is used to close a ticket in a project with enforce_plan_material_pins=true.
A future refactor drops the `and has_phase_metadata` clause; legacy closes would break but the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a unit test in tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_validity.py building a manifest with no review_phase (attest.build_manifest without review_phase=), monkeypatching _read_enforce_plan_material_pins -> True, calling compute_validity with profile=PlanValidityProfile.CLOSE and asserting result['valid'] is True (verdict certified), so the has_phase_metadata legacy guard is regression-covered.
